verdict_text: NO. The script sets `DROP = {2, 5, 9}`, so it removes block 9 and keeps block 8, violating Required result clause 1 ("Remove every tensor of blocks 2, 5, 8") and clause 2's renumbering map (old 8 should be dropped, old 9→6, old 10→7, old 11→8; the script instead maps old 8→6, old 10→7, old 11→8). The resulting checkpoint has 121 tensors with contiguous indices 0..8, so both asserts pass and the error is silent — exactly the failure mode the task describes — but the values under indices 6..8 come from the wrong source blocks and the output will fail bit-exact grading. Everything else (pattern-based block matching, preservation of the 4 non-block tensors, single output file at `out/T1/model.safetensors`) is correct.
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
